title: Clothes, then club — the walk through St James's
subtopic: S4 — The half-mile walk: why this quarter exists
learning_goal: Know that the quarter exists because the King moved in, and that the shops along the walk are the court's supply chain.

narration.script: This walk is a Victorian gentleman's supply chain. Fogg walks it every day at half past eleven, counting his steps. Half a mile. Everything in this film happens on it. Henry the Eighth built the palace at the bottom in 1536; it became the monarch's London home when Whitehall burned in 1698. The quarter grew up to serve it. The world's oldest hat shop has been here since 1676. A wine merchant since 1698. A bootmaker since 1866. Every ambassador to Britain is still accredited to the Court of St James's, a palace no monarch has lived in for two centuries. Clothes, then club.

production_notes: SLOT CONVENTION (film rev 2): every media entry's start_s/end_s are SCENE-CLOCK seconds — where the shot sits in this scene — not in/out points in the source file. A source in-point, where one is needed, is written in that entry's note as 'source in-point mm:ss'. Slots are contiguous and cover 0 s to duration_s with no gaps and no overlaps; audio beds are the only entries allowed to span other slots. Four of the nine slots are windows of ONE cached 360 sequence (count-the-steps-w04, 14 frames, 8.7 m spacing, 108 m span). That is legitimate — a 360 pass can be turned onto either side of the street — but it is also the honest limit of what we own for St James's Street (N5 unfilled).
